rmb_to_hkd_note: Approximate mid-market rate as of mid-2026. Used to convert RMB intrinsic value per share to HKD for comparison against the HKEX-listed price. All DCF inputs and outputs are in RMB millions unless labelled HKD.
revision_note: REVISED 2026-07-01 following external review. Four substantive changes: (1) Base-case FCF is no longer a flat 5.5% margin from Year 1 — it now ramps out of the capex cycle from an OCF/capex build (FY2026 FCF margin -7%, FY2027 -1%, FY2028 +2.5%, FY2029 +4%, FY2030 +5.5%), so early value is no longer front-loaded while BYD is still burning cash. (2) Terminal FCF margin capped at 4.6% (BYD's best-ever, FY2024) rather than 5.5%. (3) Equity bridge now deducts the market value of the ~34.2% BYD Electronic (0285.HK) minority (~RMB 17bn), since the consolidated DCF captures 100% of BYDE's cash flows. (4) Net-debt line now includes RMB 54.5bn of financial assets held for trading, moving BYD to a small NET CASH position (~+RMB 10bn) rather than -RMB 42bn net debt. Net effect: base case falls from HKD 81.80 (+12.6%) to HKD 53.75 (-26.0%) — the stock now screens as ABOVE base-case fair value, with a margin of safety only in the bull scenario.

inputs.shares_note: Post-split. BYD implemented an 8-for-10 bonus share distribution and 12-for-10 capital reserve capitalisation in July 2025, increasing total shares from ~3.04bn to ~9.12bn (a ~3.0x factor). Use 9,117.2M for all per-share calculations. NOTE: any comparison of the current price to pre-split highs MUST be split-adjusted (divide the pre-split quote by ~3.0).
inputs.cash_note: FY2025 year-end (Dec 2025) consolidated cash & equivalents (line 7996 of the FY2025 filing, RMB 68,395M). Down from 102,257M at FY2024 due to capex cycle peak.
inputs.financial_assets_note: FY2025 year-end 'financial assets held for trading' (current assets, RMB 54,533M, up from 40,511M at FY2024). These are liquid treasury investments (money-market/structured products) and are treated as cash-like in the net-debt bridge. Including them is what moves BYD from a -RMB 42bn cash-minus-debt position to a small NET CASH position.
inputs.total_debt_note: FY2025 year-end interest-bearing debt: short-term borrowings 38,485M + long-term borrowings 60,706M + bonds payable 4,998M + lease liabilities 8,620M = 112,809M. (The prior model used 110,500M; the difference is the treatment of the current portion / leases.) Surged from ~30bn at FY2024 as overseas factory construction was funded via debt. Q1 2026 short-term borrowings rose a further 72% QoQ.
inputs.net_cash_note: NET CASH position (positive). Cash 68,395M + financial assets held for trading 54,533M - interest-bearing debt 112,809M = +10,119M net cash. RECONCILIATION: on a narrow cash-minus-debt basis BYD looks like -RMB ~44bn net DEBT (68,395 - 112,809), but the RMB 54.5bn of liquid trading financial assets more than offsets this, leaving a modest net cash surplus. Both figures are legitimate depending on how you treat the trading portfolio; the equity bridge uses the net-cash view. Either way the buffer is far smaller than BYD's historical net cash (~RMB 60bn at FY2024).
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 FCF = operating CF 59,136M minus capex 156,808M = -97,672M (FCF margin -12.2%). Negative FCF reflects capex cycle peak (overseas factory buildout: Hungary, Thailand, Brazil; domestic charging infrastructure). FCF projections build forward FCF from separate OCF-margin and capex-intensity assumptions rather than this distorted base.
inputs.byde_minority_note: BYD Company consolidates 100% of BYD Electronic (0285.HK) revenue and cash flow but owns only ~65.8%; the ~34.2% minority is deducted from equity value at MARKET value. BYDE market cap ~HK$54.7bn (July 2026) x 34.2% = HK$18.7bn = RMB 17,166M at 1.09. This is materially larger in economic substance than the RMB 12.3bn book NCI on BYD's consolidated balance sheet, and is the correct deduction for an EV->equity bridge that captures 100% of BYDE's FCF.

historical_growth.revenue_5yr_cagr_note: FY2020 to FY2025: 153,469M -> 803,965M. Reflects extraordinary NEV market penetration surge; not forward-replicable at current scale.
historical_growth.eps_5yr_cagr_note: FY2020 to FY2025, split-adjusted; distorted by FY2020 pandemic trough.
historical_growth.equity_3yr_cagr_note: FY2022 to FY2025: 111,029M -> 246,275M. Boosted by USD5.6bn H-share placing March 2025.
historical_growth.equity_5yr_cagr_note: FY2020 to FY2025; capital raise inflates.
historical_growth.fcf_cagr_note: FCF CAGRs not calculable — FY2025 FCF is negative (-97,672M). BYD's BEST-EVER FCF margin was 4.6% (FY2024: 36,094M / 777,103M). This 4.6% is used as the hard cap on the base-case TERMINAL FCF margin — the model does not assume BYD ever sustainably exceeds its own historical peak.
historical_growth.growth_rate_note: Historical revenue CAGRs (23.8%/39.3%) are not forward-replicable at RMB 804bn scale. FY2025 revenue grew only 3.5% YoY; Q1 2026 was -11.8% YoY. Forward base rate anchored on FY2026 consensus (~RMB 850-900bn, +10-12%). Growth decelerates across Y1-Y5.

base.growth_rationale: Aligned with FY2026 analyst consensus (~RMB 850-900bn, +10-12% YoY). Decelerates from Y3 as the domestic market matures. Overseas export growth (guided ~1.5M units FY2026) partially offsets domestic softness.

fcf_build.method: OCF margin minus capex intensity, per year, so FCF emerges from the capex cycle rolling off rather than being asserted flat.
fcf_build.rationale: FY2025 capex was an extraordinary ~19.5% of revenue (156.8bn). It rolls off across the forecast: 15% -> 11% -> 9% -> 8% -> 7% as overseas factory construction (Hungary, Thailand, Brazil) completes and domestic charging buildout tapers. OCF margin recovers from a depressed ~7% (FY2025) to 12.5% as operating margins stabilise and working capital normalises. The resulting FCF margin is NEGATIVE in FY2026 (-7%) and FY2027 (-1%) — BYD is still burning cash through the capex peak (Q1 2026 OCF was only +RMB 2.8bn) — turning positive only from FY2028 and reaching 5.5% at the FY2030 exit. This deliberately removes the front-loading of value that a flat 5.5%-from-Year-1 margin created.

base.terminal_fcf_margin_rationale: Capped at 4.6% — BYD's BEST-EVER FCF margin (FY2024). Although the FY2030 exit-year FCF margin reaches 5.5%, the perpetuity value is computed on 4.6% so the terminal cash flow does not extrapolate an above-historical-peak margin forever.
base.wacc_rationale: 11%: risk-free ~4.0% (China 10yr govt bond), equity risk premium ~6.0%, China country risk premium ~1.0%. Beta ~1.0. No size discount.
base.terminal_growth_rationale: 3.0% — below Chinese nominal GDP long-run expectation; BESS global growth sustains a modestly above-inflation group trajectory.

bull.growth_rationale: Overseas exports hit ~1.5M units FY2026 (+43% YoY) and 2M+ FY2027. Hungary series production ramps through 2026, removing the 17% EU additional tariff. BESS global #1 grows 50%+ annually. Premium brands (Denza, FANGCHENGBAO) lift ASP.
bull.fcf_margin_rationale: Capex rolls off faster and OCF recovers harder than base: FY2026 FCF margin -4% (still negative — even the bull burns cash near-term), turning positive from FY2027 and reaching 7.5% by FY2030 as overseas (higher-margin) mix and electronics-AI accretion compound.
bull.terminal_fcf_margin_rationale: 6.0% terminal — above the 4.6% historical peak but justified in the bull world by a structurally higher-margin overseas revenue mix. Still below the 7.5% exit margin.
bull.wacc_rationale: 10%: overseas diversification reduces China concentration risk; Hungary normalises EU tariff exposure.
bull.terminal_growth_rationale: 3.5%: BESS leadership + overseas auto expansion sustains above-GDP trajectory.

bear.growth_rationale: Q1 2026 -11.8% YoY persists through H1; recovery modest and uneven. Domestic share erodes from 21% toward 18% as Xiaomi YU7, Geely/Zeekr, Leapmotor and Huawei-backed Aito attack simultaneously. EU tariff mitigation delayed. Price war compresses ASPs.
bear.fcf_margin_rationale: Capex stays elevated for overseas ramp + Flash Charging rollout + R&D >63bn/yr while OCF stays weak. FCF margin is negative for three years and only creeps to 2.5% by FY2030 — a prolonged cash-burn scenario, though not permanent.
bear.terminal_fcf_margin_rationale: 3.0% terminal — well below the 4.6% historical peak, reflecting structural Chinese-EV overcapacity permanently suppressing returns.
bear.wacc_rationale: 12%: short-term borrowings +72% in Q1 2026; total debt rising; FX losses on RMB strength; deteriorating domestic profitability raises risk premium.
bear.terminal_growth_rationale: 2.5%: below-GDP as commoditised EV dynamics suppress long-term returns.

base.note: At HKD 72.65, the base case implies HKD 53.75 — the stock trades ~26% ABOVE base-case fair value. With early FCF depressed by the capex cycle (negative in FY2026-27), the terminal margin capped at BYD's best-ever 4.6%, and the BYDE minority deducted, there is NO margin of safety in the base case. The prior +12.6% headline was an artefact of front-loading a flat 5.5% FCF margin and omitting the minority.

bull.note: Bull case HKD 120.82 (+66%). Requires overseas 1.5M+ units, FCF margins reaching 7.5% by FY2030, and WACC re-rating to 10%. This is the ONLY scenario offering meaningful upside from current levels. Note the bull tail is now +66% (not the prior +125%) because early FCF is depressed and the minority is deducted — the previous +125% was inflating the probability-weighted figure.

bear.note: Bear case HKD 13.56 (-81%). A prolonged cash-burn scenario: FCF negative for three years, terminal margin only 3.0%. Illustrates downside severity if the capex cycle does not resolve and domestic share keeps eroding.

base.note: To earn 15% CAGR to the base terminal value (HKD 86.76), entry must be HKD 43.14 — 41% below current. The current price does not offer a 15% return on base assumptions, consistent with the base IV of HKD 53.75 being below the current price.

bull.note: Bull terminal value implies you could pay up to HKD 82.58 today and still earn 15% CAGR — i.e. the current HKD 72.65 clears the 15% hurdle ONLY if the bull case materialises.

bear.note: Bear terminal value implies a 71% decline would be required to earn 15% CAGR.

sensitivity.note: Base-case growth [10,10,9,8,7%] and the ramped FCF path (terminal margin 4.6%) held constant; only WACC and terminal growth vary. Values in HKD per share. The current price HKD 72.65 is NOT reachable at the base WACC of 11% for any terminal growth in range (max 61.7 at TG 4.0%) — the market is discounting BYD at closer to 9-10% and/or pricing in the bull FCF path.
sensitivity.current_price_marker: HKD 72.65 aligns with WACC=9%/TG=2.5% (72.0) or WACC=10%/TG=4.0% (75.1). To justify the current price on the base FCF path you must assume a discount rate near 9-10% — i.e. the market is pricing out much of the execution/leverage risk that the 11% base WACC embeds.

probability_weighted.note: Bull 25% / Base 50% / Bear 25%. Probability-weighted IV HKD 60.47 implies -16.8% (DOWNSIDE) from HKD 72.65. This flips the prior +23.7% and is more trustworthy: the prior figure was inflated by a +125% bull tail, which the revised model reduces to +66%. TREAT WITH CAUTION REGARDLESS — the distribution is wide (bear -81% to bull +66%) and a mean across such fat tails is a weak central estimate. The BASE case (HKD 53.75, -26%) is the more reliable central anchor; the probability-weighted number is shown only to characterise the asymmetry, which is now roughly balanced-to-negative rather than the prior bullish skew.

reasonable_ranges.pe: 15-40x (growth-decelerating EV + battery + BESS; not pure-play auto at 8-12x, not pure-play growth at 50x+)

checks.comment: Base IV implies a 13.8x P/E on FY2025 earnings — modestly BELOW the 15-40x range. This reflects the conservative depressed-FCF ramp and terminal-margin cap; it is a deliberately cautious valuation rather than an error. The current market P/E of 18.6x sits comfortably inside the range.
6.6x is at the low end but within range — consistent with a capital-intensive, capex-cycle-peak business valued cautiously.
0.56x is reasonable for a low-margin, high-volume manufacturer.

sanity_check.overall_assessment: The revised base case of HKD 53.75 implies undemanding multiples (13.8x P/E, 6.6x EV/EBITDA, 0.56x P/S) — appropriately conservative given the front-loaded cash burn, the 4.6% terminal FCF-margin cap, and the BYDE minority deduction. The current traded price of HKD 72.65 (18.6x P/E, 9.5x EV/EBITDA, 0.76x P/S) is itself within reasonable ranges but sits ABOVE the base-case fair value: the market is pricing a partial bull-case recovery. No auto-correction warranted — the gap is a genuine valuation signal, not a modelling artefact.
sanity_check.ebitda_estimate_note: FY2025 EBITDA estimated as operating income (40,185M) + D&A estimate (~28,139M; ~3.5% of revenue). Official D&A not separately disclosed.

valuation_philosophy.approach: Revenue-based DCF with FCF built bottom-up from OCF margin minus capex intensity (so FCF emerges from the capex cycle rolling off), EV->equity bridge including net cash and a market-value BYDE minority deduction.
valuation_philosophy.rationale: BYD's FY2025 FCF was -97,672M due to an extraordinary capex cycle. Rather than assert a flat normalised FCF margin (which front-loads value while the company is still burning cash), the model projects OCF margin and capex intensity separately each year. Capex falls from ~19.5% of revenue (FY2025) to 7% by FY2030; OCF margin recovers from ~7% to 12.5%. The resulting FCF is negative in FY2026-27 and only reaches 5.5% at the FY2030 exit, with the perpetuity capped at BYD's best-ever 4.6%. This is materially more conservative than the prior model and removes its front-loading bias.
key_changes_from_prior_model: FCF margin: was flat 5.5% from Y1; now ramps -7% / -1% / +2.5% / +4% / +5.5% (built from OCF margin minus capex intensity).
Terminal FCF margin: was 5.5%; now capped at 4.6% (FY2024 best-ever).
Equity bridge: now deducts RMB 17.2bn market value of the ~34.2% BYD Electronic minority.
Net debt: was -RMB 42bn (cash minus debt); now +RMB 10bn NET CASH after including RMB 54.5bn financial assets held for trading.
key_risks_to_model: Capex cycle extending beyond FY2027 (Turkey, additional China charging) — would push the FCF turn further out and lower the base IV.
OCF-margin recovery to 12.5% failing to materialise if domestic price war persists.
FX losses from RMB appreciation persisting as overseas mix exceeds 40%.
EU regulatory risk delaying Hungary factory tariff relief.
BYDE minority deduction sensitivity: at BYDE's fair-value estimate (~HK$37) rather than the current ~HK$29, the deduction would be larger (~RMB 22bn), reducing base IV by a further ~HKD 0.6/share.
valuation_philosophy.currency_note: All DCF inputs and cash flows are in RMB millions. Per-share IV is calculated in RMB then converted to HKD at 1 RMB = 1.09 HKD for comparison against the HKEX H-share price.
valuation_philosophy.warning_banner: REVISED (Jul 2026). Base case now HKD 53.75 (-26%): stock trades ABOVE base-case fair value. Margin of safety exists ONLY in the bull scenario (overseas 1.5M+ units, FCF margins to 7.5%). Q1 2026 was a significant miss (Rev -11.8%, Net Profit -55% YoY) though largely FX-driven; Goldman Sachs calls it the likely trough. Base case requires monitored re-validation through Q2 2026 results.

key_observations: REVISED base case: HKD 53.75, which is ~26% BELOW the current HKD 72.65 — the stock trades ABOVE base-case fair value and offers no margin of safety on base assumptions. The prior model's +12.6% upside was an artefact of (a) a flat 5.5% FCF margin front-loaded from Year 1 while BYD is still burning cash, (b) omitting the BYD Electronic minority, and (c) counting -RMB 42bn net debt without the offsetting RMB 54.5bn of financial assets.

FCF is projected NEGATIVE in FY2026 (-7% margin) and FY2027 (-1%) — consistent with FY2025 FCF of -RMB 98bn and Q1 2026 operating cash flow of only +RMB 2.8bn — turning positive only from FY2028 and reaching the FY2030 exit margin of 5.5%. The terminal perpetuity is capped at 4.6%, BYD's best-ever (FY2024) FCF margin.

The equity bridge deducts the market value of the ~34.2% BYD Electronic (0285.HK) minority (~RMB 17bn), because the consolidated DCF captures 100% of BYDE's cash flows. This is larger in substance than the RMB 12.3bn book NCI and reduces base IV by ~HKD 2.1/share.

Net-debt reconciliation: on a narrow cash-minus-debt basis BYD looks like ~-RMB 44bn NET DEBT, but including RMB 54.5bn of financial assets held for trading leaves a small ~+RMB 10bn NET CASH position. The equity bridge uses the net-cash view; either way the buffer is far thinner than the ~RMB 60bn net cash BYD held at FY2024.

The bull case (HKD 120.82, +66%) is the only scenario with meaningful upside and requires overseas deliveries of 1.5M+ units in FY2026 with FCF margins recovering toward 7.5%. Note this is DOWN from the prior +125% bull tail — the earlier extreme was inflating the probability-weighted estimate.

The probability-weighted IV (HKD 60.47, -16.8%) now implies DOWNSIDE, flipping the prior +23.7%. It should still be treated with caution given the wide distribution (bear -81% to bull +66%); the base case (HKD 53.75) is the more reliable central anchor.

Sensitivity: at the base 11% WACC, no terminal-growth assumption in range reaches the current price (max HKD 61.7). Justifying HKD 72.65 on the base FCF path requires a ~9-10% discount rate — i.e. the market is pricing out much of the execution and leverage risk embedded in the 11% base WACC.

The 15% CAGR entry price on base assumptions is HKD 43.14 (41% below current); the bull-case entry is HKD 82.58 (above current), meaning buyers today clear a 15% hurdle only if the bull case plays out.
Q2 2026 results (expected August 2026) are the critical near-term catalyst — Citigroup estimates core net profit could recover to ~RMB 11.3bn, which would confirm the Q1 trough thesis.

De-rating context (CORRECTED): BYD's ~HK$415 pre-split peak in mid-2025 is equivalent to ~HK$138 on a split-adjusted basis (3.0x bonus/capitalisation). From that split-adjusted peak, the current HK$72.65 is a de-rating of roughly -47%, NOT the -82% that results from erroneously comparing today's post-split price to the pre-split quote.

May 2026 data point: overseas hit a record 160,644 units (+80.4% YoY), 42.6% of monthly sales mix — the first time overseas exceeded 40%. A genuine positive that partially validates the bull export thesis, but not enough to close the base-case valuation gap on its own.

Q1 2026 profit drop was largely an FX swing (finance line swung ~RMB 4bn from net income to net expense as the RMB strengthened) rather than pure operational collapse — an important nuance, but the model treats the capex-driven cash burn, not the FX item, as the central valuation driver.
